actions.name: 哑铃/弹力带肘屈曲
actions.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: a single independent rehabilitation exercise photograph PNG. The three supplied photographs are STRICT references for the exact SAME East Asian woman, her face, apparent age, skin tone, black low ponytail, plain white fitted short-sleeved T-shirt, dark charcoal full-length athletic pants, soft photographic light, realistic skin and cloth textures. Keep her facial identity and visual style consistent with ALL three references. Keep the exact pale cool gray-blue softly mottled photography backdrop color, seamlessly extended into the floor. Real studio photography, no illustration. Normal natural adult body proportions, about seven to eight heads tall, natural arms and legs, realistic five-finger hands. Portrait 1122 x 1402 PNG, same 4:5 aspect as references. ONE woman only, one continuous camera photo, no duplicate figures, no collage, no inset, no arrows, no labels, no printed words, no graphics, no watermark. Keep full head and face, all participating limbs and equipment clearly visible. Full body and feet where feasible with useful frame margins. Gray low-key necessary exercise equipment only. White unbranded simple trainers permitted. No extra people, room, shelves or decorative objects.
Exercise 174: standing single-arm dumbbell elbow flexion, SUPINATED palm-up biceps curl. The woman faces right in a slightly three-quarter near-side profile consistent with the reference face; show the working near-side arm clearly. Stand steadily with feet comfortable hip width, knees natural, upright torso and neck, no leaning back, no swinging. Hold ONE small light matte gray dumbbell in the working hand. The working upper arm is vertical and closely beside the torso; the elbow bends about 100 degrees, bringing the forearm and light dumbbell toward the shoulder. The working forearm is slightly above horizontal; the palm faces UP to the ceiling, not a neutral hammer grip. Wrist is straight and naturally aligned with forearm, no wrist curl. The other arm hangs relaxed with empty hand. Relax shoulders, no shrug and no raising the upper arm in front of the body. Make the entire dumbbell, elbow, wrist, palm-up grip and hand anatomically clear. Full body including both feet, studio floor and generous margin. No extra weights or bands.

actions.phase: 站位单手轻哑铃掌心向上肘屈曲约100度阶段，上臂靠身、手腕自然，躯干直立。

actions.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: a single independent rehabilitation exercise photograph PNG. The three supplied photographs are STRICT references for the exact SAME East Asian woman, her face, apparent age, skin tone, black low ponytail, plain white fitted short-sleeved T-shirt, dark charcoal full-length athletic pants, soft photographic light, realistic skin and cloth textures. Keep her facial identity and visual style consistent with ALL three references. Keep the exact pale cool gray-blue softly mottled photography backdrop color, seamlessly extended into the floor. Real studio photography, no illustration. Normal natural adult body proportions, about seven to eight heads tall, natural arms and legs, realistic five-finger hands. Portrait 1122 x 1402 PNG, same 4:5 aspect as references. ONE woman only, one continuous camera photo, no duplicate figures, no collage, no inset, no arrows, no labels, no printed words, no graphics, no watermark. Keep full head and face, all participating limbs and equipment clearly visible. Full body and feet where feasible with useful frame margins. Gray low-key necessary exercise equipment only. Exercise 176: forearm-supported DUMBBELL WRIST EXTENSION, palm DOWN. The woman sits naturally upright on a stable simple gray chair, facing right in a near-side view with a slight front angle to reveal the back of the working hand. Keep the complete head and face and a normal seated body proportion. A low-key gray table at comfortable seated elbow height sits beside/in front of her to the RIGHT. The entire working forearm from the elbow to just before the wrist rests firmly along a soft thin gray pad on the tabletop, horizontal and fully supported. PALM FACES DOWN toward floor, BACK OF HAND and dorsal finger knuckles face UP and are visible. Working wrist extends beyond the right edge of table and pad; the hand does not rest on tabletop. The hand securely holds ONE very small light matte gray dumbbell, modest enough to see hand and wrist anatomy. Raise ONLY the back of the hand up by about 25–30 degrees in wrist EXTENSION relative to the supported horizontal forearm, while forearm and elbow remain fully on the pad. This is a small upward bend at wrist, NOT an elbow curl, NOT an upward palm wrist flexion. Fingers naturally wrap the handle, thumb opposable and visible, five fingers, wrist connected normally; no detached, reversed or extra hands. The other hand rests on her lap and does not assist. Table must not hide the working wrist, hand, elbow or dumbbell; compose with the arm and wrist large enough to understand while preserving full face and natural seated torso, leg and chair scale. Show complete participating arm, full face and feet if framing permits. No hand inset, no arrows, no labels.
